fixes.explanation: Scripture, yes. John says it happened "…to fulfill the Scripture…" and then he quotes: "They divided My garments among them, and cast lots for My clothing." A similar line is in Psalm 22:18. It's a verse you can find in your own Bible, baker.

Those are the words. John writes, "When Jesus had received the sour wine, He said, “It is finished.” And bowing His head, He yielded up His spirit." That's a heavy part, so I'll let John's own words stand.
Golgotha is the one. John says the Place of the Skull "…in Hebrew is called Golgotha." It's a name that sticks with you. You read it right, baker.

Gethsemane is a real place, but it's a different spot. It's where Jesus went to pray before He was arrested (Matthew 26:36-50). John 19:17 gives the Hebrew name for this place as Golgotha. I'll admit those two names look like cousins at first glance.

Bethesda is a pool in Jerusalem, where Jesus healed a man who had been an invalid for thirty-eight years (John 5:2-9). That's a whole other scene. The place where Jesus carries His cross is Golgotha, and John says it right there in the verse. Don't worry, baker. I once mixed up two jars on my own shelf.

That title isn't on this notice. Pilate's sign says: "JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS." John gives us the exact words, so we don't have to guess. Sometimes a title sounds right because it sounds important, and I've done that with my own recipes.
The city, yes. John says "…the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city…" That's why "Many of the Jews…" read the sign. Being near the city is the reason John gives.
John doesn't say temple. He says the place was "…near the city…" That nearness is why many of the Jews read the sign. I get why temple jumped out at you.

The text says Pilate holds his ground. When the chief priests ask for a change, he answers, "What I have written, I have written." So the sign stays just as it was. If you were hoping for a rewrite, I get it, but Pilate doesn't change a word.
John doesn't say they leave it behind. The soldiers say, "Let us not tear it. Instead, let us cast lots to see who will get it." So the plan is to cast lots, not to leave it at the cross.

John doesn't call it a custom. He says the soldiers did it "…to fulfill the Scripture…" He then quotes from it, and a similar line appears in Psalm 22:18. Custom sounds like a reasonable guess, but John points to the Word.

A decree is a king's order, and John doesn't use that word here. He says it was "…to fulfill the Scripture…" and a similar line is found in Psalm 22:18. So it points back to the Scriptures, not to a Roman order.
Mother, yes. Jesus says to the disciple, "Here is your mother." The words mirror what He just told His mother, "Woman, here is your son." You followed the whole exchange, baker.

No ladder in this verse. John says a jar of sour wine was sitting there, and they "…soaked a sponge in the wine, put it on a stalk of hyssop, and lifted it to His mouth." The sponge on the hyssop stalk does the lifting.

John doesn't record that line here. When Jesus had received the sour wine, He said, "It is finished." Then, bowing His head, He yielded up His spirit. It's a heavy part, so I'll let John's words stand.
